issue: Microstutter at converted AAC audio segment boundaries
cause: Independent AAC encoding retained encoder priming and padding at every cut, causing overlapping timestamps and audible silent dips.
Millisecond Matroska packet timestamps and insufficient decoder context could also shift the waveform at a cut.
changes: Place every AAC piece on one 48 kHz / 1024-sample clock.
Decode and encode bounded real audio before and after each cut; remove priming and padding after encoding.
Recover the sample clock from indexed Matroska packet timestamps when they fit a constant rate, preserving real timing discontinuities.
Normalize 44.1 kHz inputs before sample-based trimming.
Use the same path for individual, batched, and compatible-audio remux requests.
Track batch audio processes for immediate cancellation when playback stops.
Version AAC caches and saved probe metadata so old audio cannot hide the fix.

includes: existing playback lifecycle and HTTP checks

performance.encoding: One FFmpeg process per requested piece, or the existing shared process for a batch.
performance.context: Bounded decoder/encoder context reuses indexed source blocks.
performance.timing_scope: Local audio preparation only; not browser startup or production seek latency.

limits: Native UI checks verify rendering, seeking and stalls; decoded synthetic waveform checks verify silent dips and clicks.
Live source checks verify decodability and packet continuity, not a listening test on the user’s exact device.
after_update: Reopen the converted stream to replace any audio already buffered by the player.
